coverage.main: Read all sixteen pages of arXiv 2003.01279v3 (27 April 2020): Sections 1-5, Tables 1-6, Figures 1-7 and references. The ECCV Workshops version of record (Springer, DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-66823-5_14) was not retrieved.
coverage.supplement: No appendix or supplement is included or referenced.
coverage.excluded_results: Tables 1-3 and 6 are white-box disruptions of the attacked generator, including white-box attacks on adversarially trained and blur-defended StarGAN (Table 6). Table 5 (identity objective) reports mean distances without a disruption rate. Figures 1-3, 5 and 7 are qualitative. No experiment transfers a disruption between different generator models.

result_groups.population: GANimation on 50 random CelebA images x 80 action units (4,000 disruptions); disruptions computed for an incorrect conditioning class, iteratively or jointly over classes, and evaluated on the generator under other conditioning classes
result_groups.outcome: % disrupted: share of outputs with L2 distance >= 0.05 from the undisrupted output G(x, c)
result_groups.evidence: The same generator is used; transfer is across conditioning classes. A clean-correct event is not defined for a translation output, and no source-success rule is stated.

result_groups.population: StarGAN test images; disruptions computed without knowledge of the deployed blur (naive, spread-spectrum, EoT) and evaluated on the generator behind Gaussian or box blur of varying magnitude
result_groups.evidence: Graphical proportions; the evaluated system differs from the attacked one only by an unknown preprocessing step. No population rule stated.

f1.evidence: Disruption is measured against the undisrupted output itself, so a clean accuracy is not defined. Table 5 includes a no-disruption baseline for the identity objective.

f2.evidence: No clean-correct analogue is defined for either scope.

f3.evidence: Neither scope states whether disruptions that fail on the attacked configuration are retained.

f4.evidence: One-decimal percentages over 4,000 disruptions do not identify unique counts; Figure 6 is graphical.

f5.evidence: L-infinity epsilon = 0.05 is explicit for class-transferable disruptions (80 PGD iterations); the budget used for the Figure 6 blur-evasion disruptions is not stated (Eq. 14 uses epsilon as the step size).

f6.evidence: The official repository contains attack code for all four architectures, including class-transferable and spread-spectrum attacks. Pretrained checkpoints come from upstream implementations and the 50 random images are not listed. Not executed.

artifact_checks.result: Linked in the paper. Listed via the GitHub API (257 files, head 7 May 2020): cyclegan/, ganimation/, pix2pixHD and StarGAN code with attacks.py modules; README describes FGSM/I-FGSM/PGD, class-transferable attacks, adversarial training and spread-spectrum evasion. Not executed.

bounds_checks.reason: Output-distortion thresholds on an image translation network are not a misclassification probability.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. Transfer across conditioning classes and unknown blur on the same generator is retained as an in-scope 'other attack outcome', as for rank 35. An independent recoder could treat the paper as having no cross-model evaluation.
